title: The Pentateuch
description: An in-depth study of Genesis through Deuteronomy - the Torah, foundation of the whole Bible. Students examine authorship and composition, the literary structure and theology of each book, creation and fall, the patriarchal covenants, the exodus and Sinai, the tabernacle and sacrificial system, holiness and law, the wilderness, and Deuteronomy's covenant renewal, with attention to how the New Testament reads the Torah in Christ.

quiz_bank.question: What is the overall purpose of the Pentateuch?
quiz_bank.answer_key: To tell the story of God's creation and covenant purposes - from creation through the patriarchs, exodus and Sinai to the plains of Moab - establishing Israel's identity as God's redeemed people, giving the law, and pointing to the promise to bless all nations.

quiz_bank.answer_key: Animals were cut in two; normally both parties walked between them, invoking a curse on themselves if they broke the covenant (cf. Jer 34:18). Only God, symbolized by the fire pot and torch, passes through - taking the oath on himself and guaranteeing the promise.

quiz_bank.question: Compare two Christian frameworks for the role of the Mosaic law.
quiz_bank.answer_key: E.g. Reformed - one covenant of grace in different administrations; moral law continues as a guide, civil and ceremonial fulfilled. Lutheran - law and gospel distinction; law accuses and guides but is not the means of righteousness. Dispensational - Mosaic covenant for Israel, church under the law of Christ. quiz_bank.question: What does Augustine mean by 'the letter kills'?
quiz_bank.answer_key: The law alone, commanding without giving the power to obey, reveals sin and condemns; the Spirit pours God's love into the heart so that the law is fulfilled from love - the law written on the heart.
